Soft Start: The instrument accelerates gradually to the set speed. That gradual ramp prevents splashing, erratic starts, and the abrupt movement of the stirring rod that throws it out of coupling and can damage a delicate preparation.

Patented Kera-Disk Plate: The Kera-Disk plate is made of aluminium with a ceramic coating, and it is both chemical-resistant and scratch-resistant. Its distinctive composition and colour run across the Heidolph magnetic stirrer range, and it survives the spills that ruin a lesser plate.

25 kg Maximum Permissible Load: The plate carries up to 25 kg. This matters more here than on any small stirrer, because a filled large-volume vessel approaches that figure quickly. Check your filled weight before you order.
EC Motor Drive: The left-turning EC motor provides consistent torque across the speed range and is efficient, drawing 25 W in normal operation and 1.7 W in standby.
Quiet Operation: Acoustic pressure is below 50 dB(A). In a preparation laboratory running several stirrers at once, that is the difference between background noise and a nuisance.

10-Year Warranty: After registering the instrument, Heidolph warrants the magnetic stirrer for at least 10 years. The design has been refined over decades for dependable operation in demanding environmental conditions.
Built for Continuous Operation: A certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-PLATE range, which supports long, uninterrupted preparation and dissolution runs.
IP42 Protection: The instrument carries IP42 protection to EN 60529 and is a Protection Class I device.

products.overview: Two knobs. Stir and heat. Everything else Heidolph put into the parts you do not touch.
features: Two Rotary Knobs, Direct Control: Speed and temperature are set on two rotary knobs against a scale. There is no menu, no display to read, and nothing between you and the two things you came to do.
Heating to 300 °C: The plate heats from 20 °C to 300 °C, which covers the great majority of heated stirring, dissolution, and reaction work carried out on a laboratory bench.
800 W Heating Power at 230 V: On an Indian 230 V supply the instrument delivers 800 W of heating output, which is what allows it to bring a liquid to temperature quickly rather than gradually.

PID Heating Control: The control algorithm holds the set temperature without overshooting past it. Overshoot is not a cosmetic problem, it is the difference between a controlled reaction and a spoiled one.

Separately Activated Heating: The heating function is switched on independently of stirring, and an LED in the button lights to show it is live. You cannot heat a plate by accident while reaching for the stirrer.

Optical Residual Heat Indicator: The indicator remains lit while the plate is above 50 °C. The most common burn on a hot plate stirrer happens after the heat has been switched off, and this is the feature that prevents it.
Large Safety Gap: The controls are separated from the heating plate by a large gap, so reaching for a knob does not mean reaching over a hot surface.
Die-Cast Aluminium Housing: The housing is die-cast aluminium: robust, durable, and chemical-resistant. The design is optimised to minimise operating errors as well as to survive spills.

Patented Kera-Disk Plate: The Kera-Disk surface is anodized aluminium, chemical-resistant and scratch-proof, and it transfers heat rapidly. Its distinctive colour and composition run across the Heidolph magnetic stirrer range.
25 kg Maximum Permissible Load: The plate carries up to 25 kg, including the vessel and its contents, which covers the vessel range this instrument is built for.

Temperature Probe Compatibility: With the EKT Hei-Con temperature control unit, the indication and measurement range extends from -80 °C to 350 °C. If your method needs the temperature of the medium rather than the plate, this is how you get it.
10-Year Warranty: After registering the instrument with Heidolph, the magnetic stirrer is warranted for at least 10 years, in a design refined over decades for demanding conditions.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core + Magnetic Stirrer is a Heidolph digital hot plate magnetic stirrer used for precise heated stirring, stirring gently to 1,400 rpm and heating with high precision to 300 °C. Temperature is set on an LCD display, and two selectable heating modules control how the setpoint is reached.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is Heidolph's safety and control hot plate magnetic stirrer, used for highly exothermic reactions, liquids with low ignition temperatures, materials with low melting points, and unsupervised heated runs. It heats to 350 °C with three selectable heating modes and two independent safety limits.

faqs.question: What is the settable ΔT on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The settable ΔT on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is a user-defined maximum difference between the set temperature and the actual temperature. It provides additional safety during highly exothermic reactions and unsupervised operation, where the sample itself generates heat.

faqs.question: What is the digital plate temperature limitation on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The digital plate temperature limitation on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer is a user-set ceiling on the temperature of the heating plate itself. It provides additional safety for liquids with a low ignition temperature and for materials with a low melting point.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer protect against delayed boiling?
faqs.answer: Yes, the automatic stir bar detector on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer confirms that the stir bar is turning, even when irregularities occur, which minimises the danger of delays in boiling.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert and the Core Ultimate?
faqs.answer: The two models share the same technical specification: 350 °C, 800 W at 230 V, 0.1 K resolution, two TFT displays, dual Pt1000 support, and bidirectional stirring. Heidolph documents the settable ΔT limit, the digital plate temperature limitation, separate timers, and programmable profiles on the Expert, and documents the RS232, USB A, USB B and USB C interfaces, standalone data logging, and e-Lift compatibility on the Ultimate.

faqs.question: What are the three heating modes on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer has three selectable heating modes. FAST provides rapid heating. PRECISE and PRECISE+ provide exact temperature regulation without overshoot, protecting sensitive samples.

faqs.question: What does the dual Pt1000 sensor do on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The dual Pt1000 sensor on the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer measures the temperature in the liquid and in the peripherals simultaneously, for example the sample and the bath liquid. When integrated into a process solution, control algorithms can be built between the two sensors interdependently.

faqs.question: What is the maximum temperature of the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer heats from 20 °C to 350 °C, with a setting accuracy of 1 K, at 800 W on a 230 V supply.

faqs.question: Does the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer have timers?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Hei-Plate Mix 'n' Heat Core Expert Magnetic Stirrer has separate timer functions for heating and for stirring. Together with programmable stirring and heating profiles, they allow reproducible, semi-automatic working.

sections.title: Safety limits and temperature control
sections.description: Safety limits and temperature control are delivered through a settable ΔT between set and actual temperature, a digital limitation of the plate temperature, three heating modes, an automatic stir bar detector, and dual Pt1000 sensing.
body: Two limits, and they guard against two different accidents.

The ΔT limit guards against the sample. In a highly exothermic reaction, the sample makes its own heat. You set the maximum allowable difference between the temperature you asked for and the temperature actually reached, and the instrument stops contributing to a runaway. This is the feature that makes unsupervised operation a considered decision rather than a gamble.

The digital plate limit guards against the plate. For a liquid with a low ignition temperature, or a material with a low melting point, the hazard is not the setpoint, it is the surface. A digital ceiling on the plate temperature caps it directly.

The stir bar detector guards against the bump. A stalled stir bar in a heated liquid leads to delayed boiling. The detector confirms the bar is turning even when irregularities occur, and minimises that danger.
